3°) Histology of the pulmonary lobule: The pulmonary lobule is the morphological and functional unit of the lung. It is made up of an interstitial stroma rich in blood vessels and comprising: 1. The 3 successive segments of the bronchiolar tree (bronchioles proper, terminal bronchioles and respiratory bronchioles) 2. The alveolar canals: they arise from the respiratory bronchioles with partially alveolated walls.

3. The alveolar ridges: these are the feet of insertion of the alveoli on the alveolar canals. 4. The canals and the alveolar sacs (alveoli): small polyhedral cavities whose total surface is called respiratory surface (50 to 100m2)

blocks.text: 4°) Histophysiology

protection and maintenance of the gaping air passages is ensured: - Thanks to the rigidity of the hyaline cartilage which facilitates the passage of air. It will be gradually replaced by smooth muscle.

- Thanks to the rigidity and above all the flexibility of the smooth muscle tissuee whose contraction allows the opening of the pathways and facilitates the passage of air. - Thanks to the Club cells which secrete the surfactant.

The maintenance of the air passages free and clean is done: - Thanks to the hair cells, the goblet cells, the seromucous glands which form the muco-ciliary mat. - Thanks to the MALT tissuee (free lymphocytes and lymphoid nodules) - Thanks to the alveolar cells.

pages.title: Gas exchanges (HEMATOSIS) occur by simple diffusion thanks to 4 particularities of the alveolar-capillary barrier:

blocks.text: 4°) Histophysiology
Gas exchanges (HEMATOSIS) occur by simple diffusion thanks to 4 particularities of the alveolar-capillary barrier:
? The extent of the respiratory surface (70 to 80m²)
? The length of the path traveled by the blood inside each lobule.
? The nature and thinness of the alveolar-capillary barrier.
? The surfactant liquid film which ensures the dissolution of gases and the maintenance of alveolar permeability.
E- Histology of the pleura

The pleura is a serosa which envelops the lungs, it is formed of 2 visceral and parietal layers separated by a virtual cavity or pleural cavity (0.5 to 1ml of liquid which has a lubricating role) which allows the layers to slide during respiratory movements.
Structure of the pleura
Each leaflet presents to be described under an optical microscope:
has. The mesothelium: which is made of flattened cells, spread out in a
single layer. b. The submesothelial layer: which is very thin; not including
cells or vessels (only elastic and reticulin fibers) c. The superficial fibro-elastic plane: thick blade sometimes split,
composed of elastic fibers and collagen. d. The subpleural layer: connective-elastic layer, made of

bundles of collagen, histiocytes, smooth muscle fibers, blood and lymphatic vessels. It continues in the interlobular septa, thus uniting the visceral pleura with the lung. In the parietal pleura, it contains adipose lobules. e. The deep fibro-elastic plane: has the same structure as the
3rd layer.
